title: Codegree polygon cost and minimum
statement: Let $N\geq0$ be an integer, $e:\operatorname{Fin}(N)\to\mathbf Z$ an integer tuple, and $w:\operatorname{Fin}(N)\to\mathbf R$ a real tuple. For any finite subset $s\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(N)$ define its polygon cost as $\sum (e_i+e_j)(w_i-w_j)$ over consecutive pairs in the increasing enumeration of $s$ (the sum is zero for fewer than two entries). Define $B(e,w)$ as the real infimum of the costs of all such $s$ containing both an index of value $0$ and one of value $N-1$. For $N\geq1$ this is the minimum over a nonempty finite family. For $N=0$ the admissible family is empty and the real infimum convention is $0$.
